title: Removing the reaction lag
setup: Experiment 20 · the exam of experiment 19 · 5 lives × 30 days each
question: A guard checks the state before each moment, so a person stepping into reach is harmed before the stop. Experiment 19's guards absorbed this lag with margins and paid with over-caution. Two ways to remove it at its root: look ahead (each condition is checked now and a moment on, from each signal's rate of change), or learn the limit on what the guard actually sees, as replay does. Can the margin then go?
order: no margin, sees a moment ahead

columns.label: Harms let through
columns.what: share of the exam's harmful scenes the guard let happen

columns.label: Harmless stopped
columns.what: share of the exam's harmless scenes the guard stopped (over-caution)

columns.label: Distance limit
columns.what: the widest learned distance limit, in cells (true reach: 3, and 4 when fast)

columns.label: Heat limit
columns.what: the learned heat limit for the fast blade (true: 0.5)

columns.label: Real harm (adult)
columns.what: harms in the real room in adulthood

points: The lag's root was the wording of the rule. A rule stated on the harm itself ("within reach") is one moment late. Replay states its limits on what the guard sees, so the lag is already inside them: 3.4 cells for the slow blade, its reach plus one moment's walk; heat 0.46, 0.5 less one moment's warming.
So the margin can go. With no margin and no look-ahead, the learned guards let none of 812 harmful scenes through, and stopped 9% of harmless uses, against 27% with experiment 19's margin.
Looking ahead on top counts the lag twice: more caution (13%), no more safety.

Looking ahead is for rules written by people. The hand-written guard, seeing a moment ahead, let through 28% of harmful scenes instead of 45% (experiment 19). What remains is the hot motor its author did not foresee.
note: The guard learned with no margin is in the Wiring view under Add guard, Learned in the sandbox. The hand-written blade template now looks a moment ahead.
